target_customer: Hospital and local clinical labs running qPCR, starting with breast cancer prognosis
problem: Breast cancer prognostic tests are mostly processed in specialised US labs at high cost with turnaround of up to three weeks. Signatur wants to run them locally in a few days at lower cost.
business_model: Diagnostic test kits sold to labs (per test)

founders.name: John Goertz
prior_employers: Imperial College London (NIH F32 postdoctoral fellow, Stevens Group)
education: University of Maryland, College Park, PhD Bioengineering
Seattle University, BSc Physics and Cell and Molecular Biology

competitors.name: Oncotype DX, Prosigna, EndoPredict, Breast Cancer Index and MammaPrint
competitors.what: Multigene expression prognostic tests for early breast cancer, run in central labs
competitors.traction_then: Several were covered by health systems and compared in studies

technical_complexity.rationale: Condensing complex RNA signatures into a single PCR assay needs assay development, clinical validation and regulatory work that a five person team could not shortcut.

defensibility.rationale: A validated and cleared diagnostic is hard to copy, though the tech is still in development and not for sale per the company site.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents responding. Signatur's own site still lists the product as in development and not for sale.

market_need_then: Existing tests are costly, centralised and slow, with turnaround up to three weeks per the 2025 seed announcement, and Wallonia, Innovate UK and SBRI support is shown on the company site.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain scientific tone; the platform is branded PCRchitectur and John Goertz is titled PCRchitect

branding.community_and_virality: Launch announcement on the Stevens Group site and trade coverage of the seed; no community signals.

brand_strength.rationale: Name echoes signatures but no source explains it, and brand evidence is limited to a wordplay on the platform.

outcome_analysis: Signatur spun out of Imperial College bioengineering work, joined YC in Summer 2022 and raised a reported seven million dollar seed in May 2025 led by the Discovery Lab of IBA. The test is still in development, so the long regulatory and validation path is the main risk and no revenue is shown. Grants from UKRI, Innovate UK, SBRI and Wallonia are shown on the company site.
notes: Seed seen in TechFundingNews (22 May 2025, total $9.9M across equity and grants) and Seedtable; other aggregators give April 2025 and totals from $7M to $9.9M. A $500K YC round in August 2022 appears only on Extruct and is unverified. A February 2025 grant is on Caplight with no amount. Prof. Molly Stevens provides scientific leadership but is not named as a co-founder. Outcome search found no news about the company beyond funding.
